title: Roman, Elliott, and Robert Caro: Live in Conversation

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the 50 years since The Power Broker was published, the book has endured in ways that few biographies have.
sentences.zh: 自《权力掮客》出版以来的50年里，这本书的生命力之持久，在传记作品中实属罕见。

sentences.en: First and foremost, it completely upended how the public viewed the former New York City Parks Commissioner Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 首先，它彻底颠覆了公众对前纽约市公园专员罗伯特·摩西的看法。

sentences.en: He went from being the man who built all those nice parks to an urban design villain.
sentences.zh: 他从那个建造了所有那些漂亮公园的人，变成了一个城市规划界的恶棍。

sentences.en: If you've been following along with the 99% Invisible breakdown of The Power Broker, you know what I'm talking about.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直在关注《99%隐形》对《权力掮客》的深度解析，你就知道我在说什么。

sentences.en: And you also know that last month, I was at the New York Historical Society with my co-host Elliot Kalin to interview Robert Caro, the author of The Power Broker, live on stage.
sentences.zh: 你也知道上个月，我和联合主持人埃利奥特·卡林在纽约历史学会现场采访了《权力掮客》的作者罗伯特·卡罗。

sentences.en: The New York Historical Society holds Robert Caro's archives, which include his research for The Power Broker,
sentences.zh: 纽约历史学会收藏了罗伯特·卡罗的档案，其中包括他为《权力掮客》所做的研究，

sentences.en: as well as the papers for his four-volume biography of President Lyndon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 以及他那部关于林登·约翰逊总统的四卷本传记的资料。

sentences.en: At 89 years old, Caro is still working on the fifth and final installment.
sentences.zh: 89岁高龄的卡罗目前仍在撰写第五卷，也就是最后一卷。

sentences.en: To celebrate 50 years of The Power Broker, the Society went into their archives and curated a special exhibit that is a must-see for any Power Broker reader.
sentences.zh: 为了庆祝《权力掮客》出版50周年，学会从档案中整理出了一个特别展览，任何《权力掮客》的读者都不容错过。

sentences.en: There are so many amazing documents on display.
sentences.zh: 展出的文献资料非常惊人。

sentences.en: There's Caro's handwritten notes from his interview with Lillian Edelstein,
sentences.zh: 有卡罗采访莉莲·埃德尔斯坦时的手写笔记，

sentences.en: who tried and failed to stop Moses from tearing down her home in East Tremont to make way for the Cross Bronx Expressway.
sentences.zh: 她曾试图阻止摩西拆除她在东特雷蒙特的家，以便为横贯布朗克斯高速公路让路，但最终失败了。

sentences.en: And next to that, there's notes from Caro's interview with Robert Moses on his side of the story.
sentences.zh: 在旁边，还有卡罗采访罗伯特·摩西时，关于他那一方说法的笔记。

sentences.en: You can see in his notes where Moses told Caro that the opposition was, quote, a political thing that stirred up the animals there.
sentences.zh: 你可以在笔记中看到，摩西告诉卡罗，反对意见不过是“一种政治手段，煽动了那里的动物们”。

sentences.en: There's also pages from early drafts of The Power Broker, with huge slashes through entire paragraphs made by Caro's editor, Robert Gottlieb.
sentences.zh: 还有《权力掮客》早期草稿的页面，上面有卡罗的编辑罗伯特·戈特利布用大笔划掉的整段文字。

sentences.en: Caro often says that he cut 350,000 words, around a third of his initial draft of The Power Broker,
sentences.zh: 卡罗常说他删减了35万字，大约是他《权力掮客》初稿的三分之一，

sentences.en: partly because the publisher could not bind a book that would hold that many pages.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是出版商无法装订那么厚的书。

sentences.en: It was physically impossible to release a book of that size.
sentences.zh: 出版那种体量的书在物理上是不可能的。

sentences.en: And woven throughout the exhibit are examples of Caro's famous attention to detail, which just floored Elliot and me when we saw it.
sentences.zh: 展览中贯穿着卡罗那种著名的对细节的关注，这让我们（指我和埃利奥特）在看到时感到无比震撼。

sentences.en: One of the things that I admire so much about Robert Caro's work is that he goes everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我非常钦佩罗伯特·卡罗工作的一点是，他会深入到每一个角落。

sentences.en: And that these notes here about the West Bath House at this beach.
sentences.zh: 就像这些关于这个海滩西澡堂的笔记。

sentences.en: West Bath House Beach is practically deserted at 1038.
sentences.zh: 西澡堂海滩在10点38分几乎空无一人。

sentences.en: Of course, it's V cold.
sentences.zh: 当然，天气非常冷。

sentences.en: Hank Bogak, a New Paltz student.
sentences.zh: 汉克·博加克，一名新帕尔茨的学生。

sentences.en: It's generally pretty empty here except for Tuesdays and Fridays.
sentences.zh: 除了周二和周五，这里通常都很空。

sentences.en: And it's like just how many people he must have talked to at all different levels of wherever he was.
sentences.zh: 这就像是他无论身处何地，都与各个阶层的人进行了交谈。

sentences.en: You know, I don't think he set up an appointment with this New Paltz student that works as a lifeguard at the beach.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不认为他提前预约了这位在新帕尔茨读书、在海滩当救生员的学生。

sentences.en: I think he just went and started interviewing people, and it's the way to do it.
sentences.zh: 我想他只是直接走过去开始采访，这才是正确的方法。

sentences.en: And just to have the confidence to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且要有这样做的自信。

sentences.en: I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: Just walk up to somebody and start interviewing them.
sentences.zh: 直接走过去找人采访。

sentences.en: If you're in New York City, you should definitely make a trip to the New York Historical Society to check out the exhibit.
sentences.zh: 如果你在纽约市，一定要去纽约历史学会看看这个展览。

sentences.en: And now here's Elliot and me interviewing Robert Caro live on stage.
sentences.zh: 现在，请看我和埃利奥特在舞台上现场采访罗伯特·卡罗的片段。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, everybody, for joining us tonight.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家今晚的到来。

sentences.en: I know speaking for Roman and myself, we're so excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我知道，代表罗曼和我自己，我们非常激动能来到这里。

sentences.en: We're so honored to be here with Mr. Caro.
sentences.zh: 能与卡罗先生同台，我们深感荣幸。

sentences.en: And Mr. Caro, thank you so much for joining us tonight.
sentences.zh: 卡罗先生，非常感谢您今晚能来。

sentences.en: It just means more than we can say to be talking with you.
sentences.zh: 能与您交谈，这对我们来说意义非凡，言语难以表达。

sentences.en: I know we only have about an hour.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们只有一个小时左右的时间。

sentences.en: We've got to move really faSt.
sentences.zh: 我们得抓紧时间了。

sentences.en: So, page one.
sentences.zh: 那么，第一页。

sentences.en: No, that was my dumb comedy opening bit.
sentences.zh: 不，那是我愚蠢的开场白。

sentences.en: Thank you, everybody, for indulging me with that.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家包容我刚才的表现。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: So, what I was hoping is that you could take us back to the moment before the publication of The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 那么，我希望您能带我们回到《权力掮客》出版前的那一刻。

sentences.en: Either the excerpts, The New Yorker, or the book itself.
sentences.zh: 无论是《纽约客》的节选，还是书本身。

sentences.en: Were you more concerned that no one was going to read it?
sentences.zh: 您当时更担心的是没人会读它？

sentences.en: Or that one person in particular was about to read it?
sentences.zh: 还是担心某个人会读它？

sentences.en: Well, I knew Robert Moses was going to attack it because he attacked anything he didn't like.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道罗伯特·摩西会攻击它，因为他会攻击任何他不喜欢的作品。

sentences.en: I knew he was great with words.
sentences.zh: 我知道他文笔很好。

sentences.en: Robert Moses, when he was at Yale, was a poet.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西在耶鲁大学时曾是一名诗人。

sentences.en: And he was actually a good one.
sentences.zh: 而且他确实写得不错。

sentences.en: He coined a good phrase about me, venomous viper.
sentences.zh: 他给我起了一个很贴切的绰号：毒蛇。

sentences.en: And the New York Times then would print anything Robert Moses said as fact.
sentences.zh: 当时的《纽约时报》会把罗伯特·摩西说的任何话都当作事实来刊登。

sentences.en: So, the headline was, Caro, venomous viper, comma, Moses says.
sentences.zh: 所以标题就是：卡罗，毒蛇，摩西说。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And what did that feel like when you heard venomous viper?
sentences.zh: 当您听到“毒蛇”这个称呼时，是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Were you prepared for it?
sentences.zh: 您有心理准备吗？

sentences.en: That he would attack him?
sentences.zh: 他会攻击您？

sentences.en: I mean, just like, what did it mean to be attacked by him?
sentences.zh: 我是说，被他攻击意味着什么？

sentences.en: I mean, you had done so much work.
sentences.zh: 毕竟您做了那么多工作。

sentences.en: Your opinion of him was right there in black and white.
sentences.zh: 您对他的评价就写在黑纸白字上。

sentences.en: But did it do something?
sentences.zh: 但这有什么影响吗？

sentences.en: Like, what did it feel like when you finally got that type of reaction from him?
sentences.zh: 比如，当您最终从他那里得到这种反应时，是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, you know, I was expecting the book wouldn't sell very many copies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我当时预料这本书卖不了多少本。

sentences.en: And I was sort of overwhelmed by the reception.
sentences.zh: 而读者的反响让我有些受宠若惊。

sentences.en: I'll tell you one anecdote.
sentences.zh: 我给你们讲个轶事。

sentences.en: My first review in the New York Times was not wholly favorable, you know?
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》上的第一篇书评并不完全是好评，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So, in those days, if my publisher expected you to have a lot of interviews,
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，如果出版商希望你接受很多采访，

sentences.en: they gave you an offer, someone's office who was on vacation.
sentences.zh: 他们会借用某位正在度假的人的办公室。

sentences.en: So, I was sitting in there, having digested this, you know, review.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时坐在那里，消化着那篇书评。

sentences.en: And suddenly, Joseph Heller was standing in the doorway.
sentences.zh: 突然，约瑟夫·海勒站在了门口。

sentences.en: Now, his book, Something Happened, was published the same month as The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 他的书《出了什么事》和《权力掮客》是在同一个月出版的。

sentences.en: And so, I would see him, you know, in the halls.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常在走廊里见到他。

sentences.en: But I was too much in awe.
sentences.zh: 但我对他太敬畏了。

sentences.en: I would say hello.
sentences.zh: 我会打个招呼。

sentences.en: We used to say hello.
sentences.zh: 我们过去常打招呼。

sentences.en: I was too much in awe.
sentences.zh: 我对他太敬畏了。

sentences.en: We never had had a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有真正交谈过。

sentences.en: And there he is, suddenly standing in the doorway.
sentences.zh: 结果他突然站在了门口。

sentences.en: I later figured out that Bob Gottlieb said, go in there and cheer him up.
sentences.zh: 我后来才明白是鲍勃·戈特利布让他进去给我打打气。

sentences.en: And he says, and he says, hey, hear this kind of voice.
sentences.zh: 他说，他用那种嗓音说，

sentences.en: Hey, kid, great review this morning.
sentences.zh: “嘿，孩子，今天早上的书评写得真棒。”

sentences.en: And I said something like, oh, I don't know it was so good.
sentences.zh: 我说了一些类似“哦，我不知道它写得好不好”之类的话。

sentences.en: And he said, you don't understand, he says, the only thing that matters is the space.
sentences.zh: 他说：“你不明白，唯一重要的是版面空间。”

sentences.en: This guy usually only writes this law.
sentences.zh: 那个人通常只写这么短的评论。

sentences.en: For you, he wrote this law.
sentences.zh: 为你，他写了这么长。

sentences.en: So, that's Robert Moses' reaction, negative.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是罗伯特·摩西的反应，是负面的。

sentences.en: The Times reaction, mixed.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的反应，是褒贬不一的。

sentences.en: I was wondering, the names on the cover of the book are Robert Moses and Robert Caro.
sentences.zh: 我在想，书封上的名字是罗伯特·摩西和罗伯特·卡罗。

sentences.en: But there's so many people in this book.
sentences.zh: 但书里有那么多人。

sentences.en: There's so many people whose stories you tell and whose names you bring attention to when another book might have glossed over them.
sentences.zh: 有那么多人的故事被您讲述，他们的名字被您关注，而在其他书中可能就被一笔带过了。

sentences.en: And I assume on the assumption that if everyone who's mentioned in the book buys a copy, you're good for like a couple dozen copies.
sentences.zh: 我假设如果书里提到的每个人都买一本，您至少能卖出几十本。

sentences.en: But I was wondering, had you received any reaction after publication from anyone you talked about in the book?
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，出版后您是否收到过书中提到的人的反馈？

sentences.en: Any of the people like Lillian Edelstein or anyone like that?
sentences.zh: 比如莉莲·埃德尔斯坦或者类似的人？

sentences.en: How did they feel about the way their stories were told, if you heard from them?
sentences.zh: 如果您收到过他们的反馈，他们对您讲述他们故事的方式有什么看法？

sentences.en: Oh, you know, there are a lot of people, a lot of different chapters.
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道，有很多人，很多不同的章节。

sentences.en: The most moving thing for me were the people of the Cross Bronx, the people who were thrown out for the Cross Bronx Expressway.
sentences.zh: 对我来说最感人的是横贯布朗克斯的人们，那些为了修建高速公路而被赶走的人。

sentences.en: And that morning, I had interviewed like two people, two couples.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，我采访了两个人，两对夫妇。

sentences.en: One lived in co-op city and one lived with their kids.
sentences.zh: 一个住在合作城，一个和孩子住在一起。

sentences.en: And that afternoon, I had an interview with Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，我采访了罗伯特·摩西。

sentences.en: So my first question was, what do you think the effect was on the people who lived there?
sentences.zh: 所以我问的第一个问题是：您认为这对住在那里的人有什么影响？

sentences.en: And I still remember.
sentences.zh: 我至今还记得。

sentences.en: And if I didn't remember, it's in that notebook.
sentences.zh: 如果我不记得了，那本笔记本里也记着。

sentences.en: That's what I said.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么说的。

sentences.en: Oh, he said, there was very little hardship there at all.
sentences.zh: 哦，他说：“那里几乎没什么困难。”

sentences.en: They stirred up the animals, but I just stood faSt.
sentences.zh: “他们煽动了那些动物，但我只是坚定不移。”

sentences.en: So I won.
sentences.zh: “所以我赢了。”

sentences.en: And that's not quite answering your question.
sentences.zh: 这并没有完全回答你的问题。

sentences.en: I noticed.
sentences.zh: 我注意到了。

sentences.en: I've learned from you.
sentences.zh: 我是从您那儿学来的。

sentences.en: But it's leading up to your question.
sentences.zh: 但这正是在铺垫你的问题。

sentences.en: The book is a war.
sentences.zh: 这本书是一场战争。

sentences.en: So, but over the years, over and over again, I'd be giving a talk somewhere and someone would come up to me and say, I lived on 187th Street or I lived on Southern Boulevard.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我不断地在各地演讲，总有人走过来对我说：“我住在187街”或者“我住在南大道”。

sentences.en: And I'm so glad that you told what happened to us.
sentences.zh: “我很高兴你讲述了发生在我们身上的事。”

sentences.en: So that was a reaction.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一种反应。

sentences.en: People in power were enraged at the book.
sentences.zh: 当权者对这本书感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Mayor Wagner was enraged at it and issued a really strong statement denouncing it, you know.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳市长对此非常愤怒，并发表了一份措辞严厉的声明进行谴责。

sentences.en: And you're not really used to that, to tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 说实话，你并不习惯那种场面。

sentences.en: And you keep wondering if you did something wrong, you know.
sentences.zh: 你会不断怀疑自己是不是做错了什么。

sentences.en: But it sort of faded away, I must say, rather quickly.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，那种愤怒很快就消散了。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, people were talking about the power broker in their columns or in a way that was really made me feel good.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，人们开始在专栏中谈论《权力掮客》，这让我感觉非常好。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So in the power broker, you take a lot of care as a biographer to sort of, you know, set the stage of like why Robert Moses is the way he is, talking about his mother, Belle,
sentences.zh: 在《权力掮客》中，作为传记作者，您非常细心地铺陈背景，比如罗伯特·摩西为什么会变成这样，谈到了他的母亲贝尔，

sentences.en: Belle Moskowitz as well.
sentences.zh: 还有贝尔·莫斯科维茨。

sentences.en: And in the Lyndon Johnson books, you even go deeper and you're like, what is the soil composition of the hill country to lead him to be who he is?
sentences.zh: 在林登·约翰逊的书中，您甚至挖掘得更深，比如“希尔乡村的土壤成分如何造就了他”？

sentences.en: And I wonder, this part of you, this core of you, that is so attuned to the people who have less power and so committed and driven to telling their story.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，您内心深处这种对弱势群体的关注，以及讲述他们故事的坚定使命感，

sentences.en: Where does that come from for you?
sentences.zh: 这源于什么？

sentences.en: Where did you get that impulse?
sentences.zh: 这种冲动从何而来？

sentences.en: Oh, no one's ever asked me that.
sentences.zh: 哦，从来没有人问过我这个问题。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you, it started actually on Newsday when I was still working just night and I came across, they were taking, I'm trying to think of a way, I'm editing myself now.
sentences.zh: 但我告诉你，其实是在《新闻日报》工作时开始的，当时我还在上夜班，我偶然发现……我在想怎么说，我正在自我编辑。

sentences.en: So the story will be, there's no, there's no editor here.
sentences.zh: 没关系，这里没有编辑。

sentences.en: You can finally talk at length, however long you want.
sentences.zh: 您可以尽情畅谈，想说多久都行。

sentences.en: There was a huge thing going on where con men were selling retirement home sites in the Mojave Desert, aiming at the widows of patrolmen and the PBA and firemen.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一件大事，骗子们在莫哈韦沙漠兜售退休住宅用地，目标是巡警、警察慈善协会成员和消防员的遗孀们。

sentences.en: And for some reason, I'd never done an investigative piece, for some reason it struck me that something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，我从未做过调查报道，但直觉告诉我有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And I remember I went to Alan Hathaway, who was this tough old managing editor, and I said, I'd like to go out to Arizona.
sentences.zh: 我记得我去找了艾伦·海瑟薇，他是一位强硬的老总编辑，我说，我想去亚利桑那州看看。

sentences.en: I've never done anything like this before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未做过这样的事。

sentences.en: And for some reason, he allowed, he authorized me to spend time at it.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，他批准了，授权我花时间去调查。

sentences.en: I went to the Mojave Desert and there was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 我去了莫哈韦沙漠，那里什么都没有。

sentences.en: You know, there was a, where they had pictures of the beautiful country club and the swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里有精美的乡村俱乐部和游泳池的照片，

sentences.en: There was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 但实际上什么都没有。

sentences.en: There was just a sign.
sentences.zh: 只有一个牌子。

sentences.en: This is Rio Rancho Estates or something.
sentences.zh: 写着“这是里奥兰乔庄园”之类的。

sentences.en: So I started to look into this, and I went to the county clerk's office, and I saw the vast scope of this thing,
sentences.zh: 所以我开始调查，去了县书记官办公室，看到了这件事的巨大规模，

sentences.en: that tens of thousands of people had actually bought land out there, that they could never get water from there.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人买了那里的土地，却永远无法从那里获得水源。

sentences.en: There was no water, and there was, and I didn't know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 那里没有水，我不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: I had never done a long story.
sentences.zh: 我从未写过长篇报道。

sentences.en: And I remember the next day, I was driving around the desert, and I came to the top of a rise, and there below me was an old lady carrying two buckets of water.
sentences.zh: 我记得第二天，我开车在沙漠里转悠，来到一个山坡顶上，下面是一位老妇人，提着两桶水。

sentences.en: And it appeared to me she was carrying him from nowhere to nowhere.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，她似乎是在带他从虚无走向虚无。

sentences.en: When I drove over the next rise, I saw she had sort of a corrugated oin.
sentences.zh: 当我开车翻过下一个坡时，我看到她有种波纹状的……

sentences.en: She had built sort of a corrugated tin shack.
sentences.zh: 她盖了一间波纹铁皮棚屋。

sentences.en: And I looked at her as she was coming, and I suddenly said, you know, you don't have to explain everything to people.
sentences.zh: 我看着她走过来，突然想到，你知道吗，你没必要向人们解释一切。

sentences.en: You just have to tell about her.
sentences.zh: 你只需要讲述关于她的故事。

sentences.en: And that worked as it happened, and after that, I just always felt I was attracted to the people who were hurt.
sentences.zh: 事实证明这很有效，从那以后，我总是觉得我会被那些受过伤害的人所吸引。

sentences.en: That's about all I can say.
sentences.zh: 我能说的也就这些了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you feel it in the work.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为你在作品中能感受到这一点。

sentences.en: I think it's one of the reasons why it endures, is that thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是它能流传至今的原因之一，就是那种东西。

sentences.en: Not just the story of Moses, but the story of all these other people.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是摩西的故事，而是所有这些人的故事。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: This is going to seem like a non-sequitur question after that very dramatic answer and question, but it's related in a way.
sentences.zh: 在刚才那个非常戏剧性的问答之后，这个问题听起来可能有点不合逻辑，但从某种程度上来说是有联系的。

sentences.en: Something that sticks out to me from that reporting series that you did is the picture you took where you are sitting at a table with a bottle of wine in the middle of nowhere for that Newsday article.
sentences.zh: 在那篇报道系列中，有一件事让我印象深刻，就是你为《新闻日报》那篇文章拍的照片，照片里你坐在荒郊野外的一张桌子旁，放着一瓶酒。

sentences.en: And it's a very funny picture.
sentences.zh: 那是一张非常有趣的照片。

sentences.en: And in The Power Broker, something that I feel like does not get talked about, but I guess maybe it stuck out to me because I'm a comedy writer by trade,
sentences.zh: 在《权力掮客》中，有一点我觉得没怎么被讨论过，但我想可能是因为我是干喜剧编剧出身的，所以它引起了我的注意，

sentences.en: is that there are times when it's a very funny book.
sentences.zh: 那就是这本书里有很多非常幽默的地方。

sentences.en: There's a line in it that I love so much where you're quoting Moses saying, traffic on the LIE will flow freely.
sentences.zh: 书里有一句我非常喜欢的话，你引用摩西的话说，长岛高速公路（LIE）上的交通将畅通无阻。

sentences.en: And then you just write inappropriate adverb right afterwards.
sentences.zh: 然后你紧接着写了一句“不恰当的副词”。

sentences.en: Or when you're talking, I forget which bridge or expressway it is that the press is saying this will solve traffic forever.
sentences.zh: 或者当你谈到——我忘了是哪座桥还是哪条高速公路——媒体说这将永远解决交通问题时。

sentences.en: And then there's a space.
sentences.zh: 然后留了一段空白。

sentences.en: And then afterwards it just says, it solved it for about two weeks.
sentences.zh: 接着后面写道：它解决了大约两周的交通问题。

sentences.en: And I wondered if while you were writing it,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你在写的时候，

sentences.en: there were times when you were aware of how funny those lines are and if it ever felt strange or if there were times when you were like, this book's getting a little dry,
sentences.zh: 是否意识到这些台词有多幽默，是否觉得奇怪，或者有没有觉得这本书变得有点枯燥，

sentences.en: I need to put a joke in somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我得在某个地方加个笑话。

sentences.en: Or if there's just something very New York about speaking that way and writing that way.
sentences.zh: 或者说，这种说话和写作方式本身就非常有纽约特色。

sentences.en: I was wondering if comedy ever came into your mind while you're writing it because there are very funny parts to the book.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇你在写作时是否考虑过喜剧效果，因为书里确实有非常幽默的部分。

sentences.en: Well, I wouldn't say that was a funny line.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不会说那是一句幽默的话。

sentences.en: I would say that's a line to hit hard.
sentences.zh: 我会说那是一句为了有力抨击的话。

sentences.en: You know, in my writing, I do pay a lot of attention to first lines and last lines.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我的写作中，我确实非常注重开头和结尾的句子。

sentences.en: Maybe Bob Gottlieb would say too much, you know.
sentences.zh: 也许鲍勃·戈特利布会说太注重了，你知道的。

sentences.en: But it just sort of came naturally, actually, to me.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这对我来说是很自然而然的。

sentences.en: It really feels like perhaps it's that your feeling for rhythm is so strong that you're tapping into that rhythm.
sentences.zh: 感觉确实可能是因为你对节奏的感知力太强了，所以你抓住了那种节奏。

sentences.en: Maybe I'm reading it as a comedy rhythm, but it makes it such a lively book.
sentences.zh: 也许我是把它当作喜剧节奏来读的，但这让它成为了一本非常生动的书。

sentences.en: It makes it such a living book that you have this feel for the rhythm of the words.
sentences.zh: 你对文字节奏的这种感觉，让它成为了一本鲜活的书。

sentences.en: And there was on the episode that we just recorded, I think, the chapter, was it Rumors and Reports of Rumors?
sentences.zh: 在我们刚录制的那一集里，我想是那一章，是叫《谣言与谣言的报道》吗？

sentences.en: Where you're saying, for so-and-so, it was garbage cans.
sentences.zh: 你写道，对于某某人来说，那是垃圾桶。

sentences.en: For so-and-so, it was like your opening lines are so fantastic for each of those sections in that chapter.
sentences.zh: 对于某某人来说，那是……你那一章里每一节的开场白都太精彩了。

sentences.en: Did you find it was hard to come up with those opening lines or did they come to you like a lightning bolt?
sentences.zh: 你觉得想出这些开场白很难吗？还是它们像闪电一样突然出现在你脑海里？

sentences.en: No, hard.
sentences.zh: 不，很难。

sentences.en: You know, I'm glad you used the word rhythm twice in the thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很高兴你在刚才的话里用了两次“节奏”这个词。

sentences.en: I should have used it three times.
sentences.zh: 我应该用三次的。

sentences.en: That would have been better for rhythm.
sentences.zh: 那样节奏会更好。

sentences.en: Three times.
sentences.zh: 三次。

sentences.en: Even better.
sentences.zh: 更好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, if I can just digress, people say nobody reads history anymore, you know.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，如果我能离题一下，人们常说现在没人读历史了，你知道的。

sentences.en: We're not interested in history.
sentences.zh: 我们对历史不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But the fact is, I think history is fascinating and anyone would be interested in it if it's written the way it is.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我认为历史非常迷人，如果写得像这样，任何人都会感兴趣。

sentences.en: That history is a wonderful story, very dramatic, what's happening.
sentences.zh: 那段历史是一个精彩的故事，非常戏剧性，正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: What's happening in America today, how much more dramatic can you be?
sentences.zh: 今天在美国发生的事情，还能有什么比这更戏剧性的呢？

sentences.en: It's like a horrible but fascinating movie.
sentences.zh: 就像一部糟糕但又引人入胜的电影。

sentences.en: So I have always, for some reason, felt that the rhythm of the words was very important.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直觉得，出于某种原因，文字的节奏非常重要。

sentences.en: I don't know that anybody agrees with me, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有没有人同意我的看法，你知道的。

sentences.en: But I think that more people would read history if history was written with more attention to the things that novelists, fiction writers, the rhythm of sentences,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，如果历史写作能更多地关注小说家、虚构文学作家所关注的东西，比如句子的节奏、

sentences.en: the rhythm of words.
sentences.zh: 词语的节奏，那么会有更多人阅读历史。

sentences.en: You know, there is, I believe, there is a right word for what you're trying to say.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我相信，对于你想表达的意思，总有一个最恰当的词。

sentences.en: Even if you have to spend a long time thinking about that word, looking for that word, you know.
sentences.zh: 即使你必须花很长时间去思考那个词，去寻找那个词，你知道的。

sentences.en: So if the answer to your question is, it's deliberate, you know, that's all I have to say.
sentences.zh: 所以如果对你问题的回答是，这是刻意的，你知道，我只能说这些。

sentences.en: We notice as we're talking about it on the podcast and we go chapter by chapter, one of the things I love and love, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们在播客里讨论它，一章一章地讲时注意到，我喜欢并乐于（你知道的）

sentences.en: noting and talking about is the way that each chapter has a bit of a cliffhanger to get you to read the next one.
sentences.zh: 指出并讨论的一点是，每一章都有点悬念，吸引你读下一章。

sentences.en: And it's really, I just think the wordsmithing is just so much fun.
sentences.zh: 这真的……我只是觉得这种文字打磨太有趣了。

sentences.en: It seems like very newspaper writing, just like, get you to the next thing.
sentences.zh: 这看起来非常像报纸写作，就是那种吸引你读下一段的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, I want to read the next thing, like, right now.
sentences.zh: 就像，我现在就想读下一段。

sentences.en: Well, I want them to read the next thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我就是想让他们读下一段。

sentences.en: And I also wondered, like, in terms of this.
sentences.zh: 我还想问，关于这一点。

sentences.en: Oh, could I?
sentences.zh: 哦，我可以吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, please.
sentences.zh: 好的，请讲。

sentences.en: An answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I mean, I didn't mean to.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不是故意的。

sentences.en: No, you answering the question is why we're all here.
sentences.zh: 不，你回答问题正是我们大家来到这里的原因。

sentences.en: I've said it, you know, I've said it before on television, but I don't know that any, you know, people saw it.
sentences.zh: 我说过，你知道，我在电视上也说过，但我不知道有没有人看到。

sentences.en: I mean, when I was starting the book, I do all my, and particularly on the Power Broker, I did all my research before I started the book.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当我开始写这本书时，我做所有的——特别是在《权力掮客》上，我在动笔前做了所有的研究。

sentences.en: And then I realized nobody's going to read this book.
sentences.zh: 然后我意识到没人会读这本书。

sentences.en: You know, no one really knew who Robert Moses was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没人真的知道罗伯特·摩西是谁。

sentences.en: They certainly didn't know there was an interesting story there.
sentences.zh: 他们当然不知道那里有一个有趣的故事。

sentences.en: I said, how am I going to get them to read this book?
sentences.zh: 我说，我该怎么让他们读这本书呢？

sentences.en: And I have to do an introduction that tells people what he's done.
sentences.zh: 我必须写一个引言，告诉人们他做了什么。

sentences.en: And I couldn't figure out, I mean, you talk about time.
sentences.zh: 我没法想出——我是说，你谈到了时间。

sentences.en: Days, I couldn't figure out a way to do it.
sentences.zh: 好几天，我都想不出办法来。

sentences.en: But I thought of, well, who else wrote about someone who had so much to compliment?
sentences.zh: 但我想到，还有谁写过一个有那么多成就的人？

sentences.en: Homer, you know, in the Iliad.
sentences.zh: 荷马，你知道，在《伊利亚特》里。

sentences.en: So I said, how did he do that?
sentences.zh: 所以我说，他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: And I remember I went and said, oh, he did it by listing the countries that sent ships one after the other.
sentences.zh: 我记得我去查了，哦，他是通过列举那些派遣船只的国家，一个接一个地列举出来的。

sentences.en: Somehow that draws you into the book, the rhythm in which he wrote.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，他写作的节奏把你带入了书中。

sentences.en: So I said, I'll try to do that with his highways.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，我也要试着在他的高速公路上这样做。

sentences.en: Because if you just say he built 627 miles of expressways and parkways, that's not going to get anyone to read the book.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是说他修建了627英里的高速公路和公园大道，那不会吸引任何人去读这本书。

sentences.en: So I listed them.
sentences.zh: 所以我列出了它们。

sentences.en: That didn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 那没起什么作用。

sentences.en: I said, so what's the rhythm here?
sentences.zh: 我说，那这里的节奏是什么？

sentences.en: You know, I said, what if I find a rhythm that draws people in?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我说，如果我能找到一种吸引人的节奏呢？

sentences.en: And that was a deliberate thing I was thinking of.
sentences.zh: 那是我刻意考虑的事情。

sentences.en: And I listed them over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我一遍又一遍地列出它们。

sentences.en: And they came out different.
sentences.zh: 它们出来的效果不同。

sentences.en: You know, when suddenly I saw they're coming out in a rhythm.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我突然发现它们呈现出一种节奏时。

sentences.en: Now I'm almost there, you know.
sentences.zh: 现在我快成功了，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I don't say I succeeded in getting there.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说我成功做到了。

sentences.en: But that's what I was trying to do.
sentences.zh: 但那是我当时试图做的。

sentences.en: So if you're talking about something in government or history that seems is dry.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你谈论的是政府或历史中看起来很枯燥的事情。

sentences.en: If it's dry, then it's dry.
sentences.zh: 如果它枯燥，那它就是枯燥的。

sentences.en: But if it's dramatic, if there's a man trying to put a highway through a crowded area and throw all the whatever I said in the book, 15,000 people out with no place to go.
sentences.zh: 但如果它很戏剧性，如果有一个人试图在拥挤的区域修建高速公路，并把我在书里说的那些人——15000人——赶走，让他们无处可去。

sentences.en: So you say, that's a story, and you've got to find a way to tell it as a story.
sentences.zh: 所以你会说，这是一个故事，你必须找到一种方法把它当作故事来讲。

sentences.en: And that takes a long time sometimes.
sentences.zh: 这有时需要很长时间。

sentences.en: The time, I mean, from the point of view of me, someone who did not have to do that work and just gets to read it, the time,
sentences.zh: 时间，我是说，从我这个不必做那项工作、只是有幸阅读它的人的角度来看，这些时间，

sentences.en: it seems very well worth it because the book is so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 似乎非常值得，因为这本书太美了。

sentences.en: And an indication of that, which I think we have not talked about on the podcast, is that I have a 10-year-old son, and there are nights when before he goes to bed,
sentences.zh: 一个迹象是，我想我们在播客里还没谈过，我有一个10岁的儿子，有时在他睡觉前，

sentences.en: he asks me to read him a page or two of The Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 他会让我给他读一两页《权力掮客》。

sentences.en: And he particularly likes those lists in the introduction, and he'll ask me to read him those pages, the lists of the expressways and the bridges,
sentences.zh: 他特别喜欢引言里的那些列表，他会让我读那些页面，那些高速公路和桥梁的列表，

sentences.en: and I think it's that rhythm just captures him.
sentences.zh: 我想是那种节奏吸引了他。

sentences.en: And he doesn't know those places, and it's made it very hard to continue through the book at a pace that it's going to take a while to finish reading it,
sentences.zh: 他并不了解那些地方，这使得很难以一种能很快读完的速度继续读下去，

sentences.en: a page or two at a time to him at bedtime.
sentences.zh: 睡前一次读一两页。

sentences.en: But it's such a – I feel like there's no other work of history that I can think of that my 10-year-old is asking me to read to him at bed to get him into that – and it doesn't lull him to sleep.
sentences.zh: 但这真是——我觉得我想不出还有哪部历史著作，我10岁的儿子会要求我在睡前读给他听，让他进入那种状态——而且它并没有让他昏昏欲睡。

sentences.en: I have to stop because he's not sleeping, and I have to leave the room.
sentences.zh: 我不得不停下来，因为他还没睡着，我得离开房间。

sentences.en: But it's that rhythm, I think, really captures him, even just the sounds of those words are so beautiful, the way you put them together.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，那种节奏真的吸引了他，即使只是那些词语的声音也如此美妙，你把它们组合在一起的方式。

sentences.en: Well, you just made my day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你让我今天过得太开心了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: That's something I'll remember.
sentences.zh: 我会记住这件事的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'll tell him you said that.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉他你这么说的。

sentences.en: When you're writing,
sentences.zh: 当你写作时，

sentences.en: how much are you balancing being a historian and making sure that this number is out there for people to have for all time versus moving the story forward dramatically?
sentences.zh: 你在多大程度上平衡作为历史学家的身份，确保这些数字被记录下来供后人参考，与推动故事戏剧性发展之间的关系？

sentences.en: Talk about the difficulty of that because that seems very hard.
sentences.zh: 谈谈其中的难度，因为这看起来非常难。

sentences.en: That's really hard.
sentences.zh: 那确实很难。

sentences.en: Sometimes you feel you're trapped by the fact.
sentences.zh: 有时你会觉得被事实困住了。

sentences.en: You know this is a dramatic scene.
sentences.zh: 你知道这是一个戏剧性的场景。

sentences.en: Like right now in the book I'm writing now –
sentences.zh: 就像我现在正在写的这本书——

sentences.en: Are you working on a book right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在正在写书吗？

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我一点都不知道。

sentences.en: I didn't realize it.
sentences.zh: 我没意识到。

sentences.en: No, it's about Lyndon Johnson.
sentences.zh: 不，是关于林登·约翰逊的。

sentences.en: Oh, is it?
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有意思。

sentences.en: That's a good subject.
sentences.zh: 那是个好题材。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's passing Medicare.
sentences.zh: 他正在通过医疗保险法案。

sentences.en: And it's really – it's changing the financing of the Social Security system.
sentences.zh: 这真的——它正在改变社会保障体系的融资方式。

sentences.en: And it's really dry.
sentences.zh: 这真的很枯燥。

sentences.en: It's really a lot of numbers.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多数字。

sentences.en: But more than that, it's a very complicated fight is going on in the Ways and Means Committee because the chairman, Wilbur Mills of Arkansas, doesn't want Medicare.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，筹款委员会内部正在进行一场非常复杂的斗争，因为主席，阿肯色州的威尔伯·米尔斯，不想要医疗保险。

sentences.en: And he's going to stand in – because he thinks it's going to destroy the financing of the Social Security system.
sentences.zh: 他要站出来反对——因为他认为这会摧毁社会保障体系的融资。

sentences.en: And this is a chapter about numbers.
sentences.zh: 这一章全是关于数字的。

sentences.en: And it's really dry.
sentences.zh: 这真的很枯燥。

sentences.en: But you said – it may be boastful to say – but you said, no, it's not dry.
sentences.zh: 但你说——说出来可能有点自夸——但你说，不，它不枯燥。

sentences.en: This is – all the people in the United States who had to choose between financing their – sending their kids to college and taking care of their grandparents because there is no Medicare,
sentences.zh: 这是——美国所有那些必须在资助孩子上大学和照顾祖父母之间做选择的人，因为没有医疗保险，

sentences.en: that's not dry.
sentences.zh: 那并不枯燥。

sentences.en: You have to take these numbers and find a way of weaving them into something that people understand how big this question is.
sentences.zh: 你必须拿这些数字，想办法把它们编织成人们能理解这个问题的严重性的东西。

sentences.en: So you're constantly – it's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 所以你不断地——这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I mean you're constantly – that's an extreme example.
sentences.zh: 我是说你不断地——这是一个极端的例子。

sentences.en: But you're constantly stuck by facts.
sentences.zh: 但你不断地被事实所困扰。

sentences.en: These numbers.
sentences.zh: 这些数字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you ever find – one of the things that makes your writing so powerful is there's this passion behind it.
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现——你的写作之所以如此有力，原因之一就是字里行间蕴含着那种激情。

sentences.en: There's this excitement behind it about making sure people know these.
sentences.zh: 那种想要确保人们了解这些事实的兴奋感。

sentences.en: I imagine you – like if you didn't have books, I imagine you running out into the street saying, people need to know this and just grabbing people and telling them.
sentences.zh: 我能想象你——如果不是因为有书，我能想象你冲到街上，对人们说，大家需要知道这些，然后抓住路人告诉他们。

sentences.en: Do you ever – is it hard –
sentences.zh: 你有没有——这很难吗——

sentences.en: I've never done that.
sentences.zh: 我从没那样做过。

sentences.en: Luckily, you've got the books to – you should try it sometime.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，你有书可以——你应该找机会试试。

sentences.en: It's pretty – it gets the blood racing.
sentences.zh: 这相当——这会让人热血沸腾。

sentences.en: Do you ever find you're in danger of losing that passion because you're digging through numbers or because you're struggling to find just the right words?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾感到自己有失去那种激情的危险，因为你深陷于数字之中，或者因为你正苦苦思索如何找到最恰当的词句？

sentences.en: Is it hard to maintain that sense of energy that you need to get through the book to make people interested?
sentences.zh: 要保持那种让人们对书产生兴趣所需的能量感，这很难吗？

sentences.en: You ask good questions all the time, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，你总是能问出很好的问题。

sentences.en: Because you say if you do it by concentrating on individuals, telling their stories, first place it's going to take another – an additional two weeks or two months or something.
sentences.zh: 因为你说，如果你通过专注于个人、讲述他们的故事来完成，首先，这会多花——额外两周或两个月之类的时间。

sentences.en: And you don't know how to do it when you first think of it, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且当你最初想到这一点时，你并不知道该怎么做，你知道吗？

sentences.en: What you just asked is what takes so long.
sentences.zh: 你刚才问的问题正是耗时所在。

sentences.en: I know it takes my books – you know, they're too long.
sentences.zh: 我知道我的书需要——你知道，它们太长了。

sentences.en: It takes too long.
sentences.zh: 耗时太长了。

sentences.en: But it's – I could do it a lot shorter, you know, in time and in length, you know?
sentences.zh: 但它是——我本可以把它写得短得多，你知道，在时间和篇幅上，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But it's that.
sentences.zh: 但就是那样。

sentences.en: Then my feeling is then people wouldn't read it.
sentences.zh: 然后我的感觉是，那样人们就不会读它了。

sentences.en: People wouldn't understand why it's important.
sentences.zh: 人们就不会明白为什么它很重要。

sentences.en: Do you know President Kennedy is assassinated and that night Lyndon Johnson is back in Washington.
sentences.zh: 你知道肯尼迪总统遇刺，那天晚上林登·约翰逊回到了华盛顿。

sentences.en: He's in his bed.
sentences.zh: 他躺在床上。

sentences.en: He calls Bill Moyers, Jack Valenti, and Cliff Carter, three of his young aides, and he starts talking about what he's going to do.
sentences.zh: 他叫来比尔·莫耶斯、杰克·瓦伦蒂和克里夫·卡特，他身边的三位年轻助手，开始谈论他打算做什么。

sentences.en: He says, I'm going to pass Harry Truman's health bill for him.
sentences.zh: 他说，我要为哈里·杜鲁门通过他的医疗法案。

sentences.en: Well, the story of how he passes the health bill could be a very dry story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，关于他如何通过医疗法案的故事可能是一个非常枯燥的故事。

sentences.en: It's changing votes in the Senate and in the ways of the Means Committee in the House.
sentences.zh: 这涉及参议院和众议院筹款委员会的投票变动。

sentences.en: You say, yes, but this is a really important thing in American history.
sentences.zh: 你会说，是的，但这在美国历史上确实是一件非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: It's a government trying to take care of – so how does that work out?
sentences.zh: 这是一个政府试图照顾——那么这到底是怎么运作的呢？

sentences.en: How does he get it through and how does it work out?
sentences.zh: 他是如何让它通过的，结果又如何？

sentences.en: And so you really – you spend a lot of time just staring at a piece of paper and wondering how to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的——你花了很多时间盯着一张纸，思考该怎么写。

sentences.en: More of our conversation with Robert Carroll live from the New York Historical Society coming up.
sentences.zh: 更多关于我们与罗伯特·卡罗在纽约历史学会现场的对话，即将播出。

sentences.en: So we have a few questions from the audience I wanted to run past you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一些观众提出的问题，我想向你请教。

sentences.en: You know, how do you – this is one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是如何——这是其中一个。

sentences.en: How do you hope future generations will use the Power Broker and in particular your archive that's upstairs, your 20,000 linear feet of miles of archives?
sentences.zh: 你希望未来几代人如何使用《权力掮客》，特别是你楼上的档案，你那两万英尺长的档案？

sentences.en: It's rare when an author's work is measured in linear feet.
sentences.zh: 作者的作品以线性英尺来衡量，这很少见。

sentences.en: Like what do you feel when someone's like going through that stuff that you probably meant for no one to read but yourself or Ina?
sentences.zh: 比如，当有人翻阅那些你可能只想给自己或伊娜看的东西时，你是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Oh, great question.
sentences.zh: 哦，好问题。

sentences.en: You do feel funny about that, you know.
sentences.zh: 你确实会觉得有点奇怪，你知道。

sentences.en: But you say – but there's so much in it, in the archives, that no one knows, that I want people to know.
sentences.zh: 但你会说——但档案里有太多没人知道的东西，我希望人们知道。

sentences.en: I'll give you one quick example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个简单的例子。

sentences.en: Al Smith was the governor of New York.
sentences.zh: 阿尔·史密斯曾是纽约州州长。

sentences.en: You know, Franklin Roosevelt, when he was president, said to Francis Perkins, you know, Francis, 90% of everything we did in the New Deal, Al Smith did in New York.
sentences.zh: 你知道，富兰克林·罗斯福当总统时曾对弗朗西斯·珀金斯说，你知道，弗朗西斯，我们在新政中所做的一切，90%都是阿尔·史密斯在纽约做过的。

sentences.en: New York was first in welfare, first in all the things we think of today, helping people out.
sentences.zh: 纽约在福利方面处于领先地位，在所有我们今天认为的帮助人们的事情上都是第一。

sentences.en: And it's all because of this guy, unlettered, had to drop out of school in the fifth grade, and was once called Tammany's leading henchman.
sentences.zh: 这一切都归功于这个家伙，他没受过多少教育，五年级就辍学了，曾被称为坦慕尼协会的首席走狗。

sentences.en: Says to the divorces of Tammany, I'm governor now, you have to free me, and gets all this passed.
sentences.zh: 他对坦慕尼协会的那些大佬说，我现在是州长了，你们必须放手让我干，然后他通过了所有这些法案。

sentences.en: I learned about him because he raised Robert Moses to power, okay?
sentences.zh: 我了解他是因为他把罗伯特·摩西推上了权力巅峰，好吗？

sentences.en: And I said, this is the greatest story, and I did write a lot on Al Smith, which we cut out of the power broker.
sentences.zh: 我说，这是最伟大的故事，我确实写了很多关于阿尔·史密斯的内容，但我们把它们从《权力掮客》中删掉了。

sentences.en: Now, when I was researching, I said, I'm going to try to find – there's no good book, not even a half good book on Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 当时我在做研究时，我说，我要试着找——没有一本好书，甚至没有一本半好书是关于阿尔·史密斯的。

sentences.en: So I said, well, I'm going to try to find everybody who was truly close to him, truly – not bullshit, but really worked with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧，我要试着找到每一个真正了解他的人，真正——不是胡扯，而是真正与他共事过的人。

sentences.en: So there were 14 people, as I recall, left alive.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，当时还有14个人在世。

sentences.en: And I did extensive interviewing them, typed them up as I do transcripts.
sentences.zh: 我给他们做了大量的采访，并像我平时做的那样把它们整理成文字稿。

sentences.en: And they're in that archive, and I'm hoping someone will come along and do a biography of Al Smith.
sentences.zh: 它们都在那个档案里，我希望有人能来写一本阿尔·史密斯的传记。

sentences.en: Don't look at me, Roman.
sentences.zh: 别看我，罗曼。

sentences.en: I don't know this.
sentences.zh: 我不了解这个。

sentences.en: It seems like your territory.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是你的领域。

sentences.en: I do, like, Ghostbusters stuff.
sentences.zh: 我做的是，比如，捉鬼敢死队之类的东西。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know this.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不了解这个。

sentences.en: I'm not good enough for this.
sentences.zh: 我还没达到那个水平。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But if they do it, they'll be able to talk about what it was like working with him.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们写了，他们就能谈谈与他共事是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Like, the same thing with Bell Moskowitz.
sentences.zh: 就像贝尔·莫斯科维茨的情况一样。

sentences.en: No one even knows the name Bell Moskowitz.
sentences.zh: 甚至没人知道贝尔·莫斯科维茨这个名字。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, a woman named Bell Moskowitz was arguably, I think definitely, the most powerful woman politically in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代，一个叫贝尔·莫斯科维茨的女人可以说是，我认为绝对是，美国政治上最有权势的女性。

sentences.en: Nobody even knows her name.
sentences.zh: 甚至没人知道她的名字。

sentences.en: So I also did a lot of interviewing on her.
sentences.zh: 所以我对她也做了很多采访。

sentences.en: There's so much in my archives that didn't make it into the book.
sentences.zh: 我的档案里有太多没能放进书里的内容。

sentences.en: I mean, even though I wrote it, you know, we cut out 350,000 words.
sentences.zh: 我是说，尽管是我写的，你知道，我们删掉了35万字。

sentences.en: Not so funny.
sentences.zh: 不太好笑。

sentences.en: But piggybacking off of that, Roman and I got to look at the Power Broker at 50 exhibit right before we were doing this event.
sentences.zh: 但顺着这个话题，罗曼和我在做这个活动之前，刚好看了《权力掮客》50周年展览。

sentences.en: And on the wall, there's a napkin that you wrote a note on about the women of East Tremont went to see Fiddler on the Roof.
sentences.zh: 墙上有一张餐巾纸，上面写着你关于东特雷蒙特的妇女去看《屋顶上的提琴手》的笔记。

sentences.en: And for me, someone – it was two sacred things, the Power Broker and Fiddler on the Roof in one document.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，有人——这是两件神圣的事物，《权力掮客》和《屋顶上的提琴手》出现在同一份文档中。

sentences.en: And I found myself so kind of affected by seeing it, so overcome by it.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己被看到的东西深深触动，难以自持。

sentences.en: And it made me think this is a note that Mr. Caro jotted down for his book.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到，这是卡罗先生为他的书随手记下的笔记。

sentences.en: And this book that so many people have this very deep connection to and they get very obsessed with it.
sentences.zh: 这本书让许多人产生了非常深刻的联系，他们对它非常着迷。

sentences.en: It becomes very special to them.
sentences.zh: 它对他们来说变得非常特别。

sentences.en: And they read the book and it's all they want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 他们读了这本书，这就是他们想谈论的一切。

sentences.en: And do you find that weird?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Like, I'm asking for a friend.
sentences.zh: 我是替朋友问的。

sentences.en: Do you think it's weird that people get so wrapped up in the Power Broker – in your work, but in the Power Broker especially?
sentences.zh: 你觉得人们如此沉迷于《权力掮客》——沉迷于你的作品，尤其是《权力掮客》，这很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Does that ever feel strange to you?
sentences.zh: 你对此感到奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Well, what's your question?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你的问题是什么？

sentences.en: Basically, I guess the most basic way to boil it down is do you think I'm weird for taking this book and it feeling so special to me?
sentences.zh: 基本上，我想最简单的方式来总结就是，你觉得我因为觉得这本书特别而把它看得这么重，我很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: Someone who has only read it.
sentences.zh: 一个只读过它的人。

sentences.en: I assume you're mostly thankful.
sentences.zh: 我想你大多是心存感激的。

sentences.en: But does it ever feel strange that it's become such a talisman for people?
sentences.zh: 但它成为人们心中的护身符，这让你觉得奇怪吗？

sentences.en: It just makes me feel so humble.
sentences.zh: 这只会让我感到非常谦卑。

sentences.en: You know, the 50 years pass so faSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，50年过得太快了。

sentences.en: But I ride the number one train a lot.
sentences.zh: 但我经常坐1号线地铁。

sentences.en: And Columbia students are on there.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学的学生也在上面。

sentences.en: And apparently they teach the Power Broker in a couple of courses.
sentences.zh: 显然，他们在几门课程中教授《权力掮客》。

sentences.en: So for 50 years, I said to Ina, I saw the most wonderful thing today.
sentences.zh: 所以50年来，我对伊娜说，我今天看到了最美妙的事情。

sentences.en: Another kid was reading the Power Broker.
sentences.zh: 又有一个孩子在读《权力掮客》。

sentences.en: So, on the other hand, the things that are cut out of it, you know, what you just referred to.
sentences.zh: 所以，另一方面，那些被删掉的内容，你知道，你刚才提到的那些。

sentences.en: So, as I said, everybody was thrown out and they scattered to the four winds.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，每个人都被赶走了，他们四散到天涯海角。

sentences.en: I said, how different is that from the czar destroying a steddle?
sentences.zh: 我说，这和沙皇摧毁一个犹太小镇有什么不同？

sentences.en: And we were going to see Fiddler on the roof.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正要去看《屋顶上的提琴手》。

sentences.en: And the last song is Anna Tefka.
sentences.zh: 最后一首歌是《日出日落》（Anatevka）。

sentences.en: And if you remember in the staging that I saw, they're singing Anna Tefka, Anna Tefka,
sentences.zh: 如果你记得我看到的那个舞台版本，他们在唱《日出日落》，《日出日落》，

sentences.en: a place where you know everyone you meet and you'll be in a place where you're looking for one familiar face.
sentences.zh: 一个你认识每个人的地方，你会身处一个寻找熟悉面孔的地方。

sentences.en: And I said, oh, that's – I'm going to do a chapter on that, you know.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，那是——我要为此写一章，你知道。

sentences.en: And I wrote – I evidently – I didn't remember this.
sentences.zh: 我写了——显然——我不记得这个了。

sentences.en: They showed me the – I evidently wrote that down on –
sentences.zh: 他们给我看了——我显然把它写在了——

sentences.en: You probably went to dinner after the show.
sentences.zh: 你可能在演出后去吃了晚餐。

sentences.en: Now we're thinking about it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 现在我们想起来了，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I wrote it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我写了它。

sentences.en: And so there was a chapter called One Mile Afterwards, okay?
sentences.zh: 所以有一章叫《一英里之后》，好吗？

sentences.en: We had to cut – Bob Godley, you know, he said, I think, that I cut 350,000 of the best words I ever – well, I think that's about the best chapter I ever wrote.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不删掉——鲍勃·戈德利，你知道，他说，我想，我删掉了我写过的最好的35万字——嗯，我认为那是我写过的最好的章节之一。

sentences.en: And we just cut it down to like six pages or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们把它删减到了大约六页左右。

sentences.en: But – so you have so many mixed feelings about that book.
sentences.zh: 但是——所以你对那本书有这么多复杂的情感。

sentences.en: So I have another question from the audience.
sentences.zh: 所以我还有另一个观众的问题。

sentences.en: It says, after 50 years of reflection, would you portray Moses any differently today?
sentences.zh: 它说，经过50年的反思，你今天会以不同的方式描绘摩西吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: Yeah, I didn't think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也这么想。

sentences.en: Nailed it.
sentences.zh: 说得对。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm finding myself – it's hard for me to – and this is – for the past couple days,
sentences.zh: 我发现自己——这对我来说很难——这是——在过去几天里，

sentences.en: it's been very hard for me to formulate into question form the things that I want to say to you about the book.
sentences.zh: 我很难将我想对你说的关于这本书的事情组织成问题。

sentences.en: And the – I don't – does it ever – does it ever – well, actually, I apologize.
sentences.zh: 而且——我不——它有没有——它有没有——嗯，实际上，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: Roman, you ask that.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你来问那个。

sentences.en: I get very emotional about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此非常激动。

sentences.en: This relates to the exhibit a little bit, so I'm curious about this.
sentences.zh: 这与展览有点关系，所以我对此很好奇。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: That's a great idea, Roman.
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意，罗曼。

sentences.en: Ground it in something, yeah.
sentences.zh: 把它建立在具体事物上，是的。

sentences.en: Other than my beating heart for this book, yeah.
sentences.zh: 除了我为这本书跳动的心脏之外，是的。

sentences.en: So the book is subtitled The Fall of New York.
sentences.zh: 所以这本书的副标题是《纽约的陨落》。

sentences.en: How responsible was Moses for this fall?
sentences.zh: 摩西对这次陨落负有多大责任？

sentences.en: Also, were other subtitles considered?
sentences.zh: 此外，还有考虑过其他副标题吗？

sentences.en: And I know the answer to this because I saw one of them out there.
sentences.zh: 我知道这个答案，因为我在外面看到了其中一个。

sentences.en: So talk about the subtitle, The Fall of New York.
sentences.zh: 所以谈谈副标题《纽约的陨落》吧。

sentences.en: Well, the easy answer to that is it's published in 1974.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简单的答案是它出版于1974年。

sentences.en: New York was bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 纽约当时破产了。

sentences.en: You know, when you looked into it in the book, it shows how his spending on a number of things really crippled the city's financial capacity, okay?
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你在书中深入研究时，它展示了他对许多事情的支出是如何真正削弱了城市的财政能力，好吗？

sentences.en: But that's not all I meant.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我的全部意思。

sentences.en: I meant that by the time he finished being in power,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当他结束掌权时，

sentences.en: you had a city where there were a hundred – if I have this right – 144,000 units of public housing that were built in the cheapest possible way because he wanted people who were poor to feel poor.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个城市，那里有14.4万套公共住房，它们是以最廉价的方式建造的，因为他想让穷人感到贫穷。

sentences.en: And they didn't have what LaGuardia wanted to put social workers in so that people from rural areas of the south could have someone help them, you know, get it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有拉瓜迪亚想要安置的社会工作者，这样来自南方农村地区的人们就能有人帮助他们，你知道，适应这一切。

sentences.en: So they had a city that's part of New York.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拥有一个城市，那是纽约的一部分。

sentences.en: New York is by some – the most segregated city in America.
sentences.zh: 纽约在某些方面是美国种族隔离最严重的城市。

sentences.en: You have a city where people commute to – the commuting time in New York then was by – I forget how they measured it.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一个城市，人们通勤到——当时纽约的通勤时间是——我忘了他们是怎么测量的了。

sentences.en: It was the longest commutes in the world.
sentences.zh: 那是世界上最长的通勤时间。

sentences.en: It's still pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 现在依然很糟糕。

sentences.en: Rereading the book this time, it was – I've lived in Los Angeles for a few years now, but I lived in New York for a number of years.
sentences.zh: 这次重读这本书，它是——我在洛杉矶住了几年了，但我曾在纽约住了很多年。

sentences.en: And I would read about the potential for a better subway system, and I would just think about the hours I spent waiting in trains that had stopped in tunnels in my years here.
sentences.zh: 我会读到关于建立更好地铁系统的潜力，我就会想到我在那些年里花在隧道里停滞不前的火车上的时间。

sentences.en: And it was making me so angry that it's – yeah, that this is another way the city fails its residents as a result of the things Moses was doing.
sentences.zh: 这让我非常生气，它是——是的，这是城市辜负其居民的另一种方式，是摩西所作所为的结果。

sentences.en: Yes, that's the kind of thing I meant.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我所指的那种事情。

sentences.en: And black people were still not using Jones Beach.
sentences.zh: 而且黑人仍然不能使用琼斯海滩。

sentences.en: He didn't want poor people in general and people of color in particular to use Jones Beach.
sentences.zh: 他不想让穷人，特别是少数族裔使用琼斯海滩。

sentences.en: So he did a number of things, which everyone talks about, and some academics try and put a different reason on it.
sentences.zh: 所以他做了很多事，大家都在谈论这些事，而一些学者试图给出不同的解释。

sentences.en: But the people who built it knew why he was making the overpasses too low for buses to get through.
sentences.zh: 但那些建造者知道他为什么要把立交桥修得那么低，让公交车无法通过。

sentences.en: And I remember his chief engineer, Sid Shapiro,
sentences.zh: 我记得他的总工程师西德·夏皮罗（Sid Shapiro）曾说，

sentences.en: saying this is an example of – they called them RM – this was an example of RM's wonderful foresight because we had legislation passed that buses couldn't use the parkways.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子——他们称之为RM——这是RM非凡远见的例子，因为我们当时通过了立法，禁止公交车使用公园大道。

sentences.en: But, you know, legislation can be changed.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，法律是可以修改的。

sentences.en: It's really hard to change a bridge while it went west up.
sentences.zh: 但要改建一座桥梁就非常困难了。

sentences.en: So I said to Ina, I want to see if that still works.
sentences.zh: 所以我对伊娜说，我想看看这是否仍然有效。

sentences.en: So let's say this was 1970.
sentences.zh: 假设这是1970年。

sentences.en: I don't know what year it was.
sentences.zh: 我不记得具体是哪一年了。

sentences.en: So we went out there, and we stood in Jones Beach.
sentences.zh: 我们去了那里，站在琼斯海滩。

sentences.en: There's a main parking lot, which holds 10,000 cars.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个主停车场，可以容纳10,000辆车。

sentences.en: And everybody who parks there, you know, you have to go through an overpass with three archways.
sentences.zh: 每个在那里停车的人，都必须穿过一个有三个拱门的立交桥。

sentences.en: So Ina and I stood there with two pads, and you did, like, four lines, and then across – if you go up to the second floor of this museum, there's the pad.
sentences.zh: 伊娜和我站在那里，拿着两个记事本，你画了四行，然后横着画——如果你走到这个博物馆的二楼，就能看到那个本子。

sentences.en: And there's the entire page down to the bottom under whites.
sentences.zh: 整页纸一直写到最底下的“白人”那一栏。

sentences.en: That's how many whites used it.
sentences.zh: 这就是使用它的人数，全是白人。

sentences.en: There is, as I recall, 14 Latinos and I think just five black people.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，当时只有14个拉丁裔，我想黑人只有5个。

sentences.en: So his stratagem worked.
sentences.zh: 所以他的策略奏效了。

sentences.en: So that's part of what I meant by the fall of New York, you know.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的“纽约的衰落”的一部分，你知道的。

sentences.en: We had all these vast slums living in these housing projects built as cheaply as he could build them.
sentences.zh: 我们有这么多庞大的贫民窟，住在他尽可能廉价建造的住房项目中。

sentences.en: We had an education system, which he had – you know, when he did the World's Fair, he said he would have – and the number kept going up.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个教育系统，他曾说他会——你知道，当他举办世博会时，他说他会——而且这个数字一直在增加。

sentences.en: $20 million, $40 million, $80 million would – the fair would profit, and he turned it over to the education system.
sentences.zh: 2000万美元、4000万美元、8000万美元——世博会会有利润，他会把它交给教育系统。

sentences.en: Well, as it happens, I was the reporter who found out the fair was bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，碰巧我就是那个发现世博会破产的记者。

sentences.en: So in a way – anyway, that kind of thing is what I meant.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说——总之，我指的就是那种事情。

sentences.en: Well, it's been such a delight talking with you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈真是太愉快了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for the book.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你写的这本书。

sentences.en: And when I think about this book, I know that maybe people see it as this 1,200-page book of this dastardly man, Robert Moses.
sentences.zh: 当我想到这本书时，我知道也许人们把它看作是关于罗伯特·摩西（Robert Moses）这个卑劣之人的1200页巨著。

sentences.en: But what I want people to understand,
sentences.zh: 但我希望人们明白的是，

sentences.en: the pleasure of the book is spending 1,200 pages with this kind humanist who cares about this city and this country and this world in the form of you.
sentences.zh: 这本书的乐趣在于，能花1200页的时间与你这样一位仁慈的人文主义者相处，你以自己的方式关心着这座城市、这个国家和这个世界。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that it makes it so – I think that's one of the things that makes it endure for 50 years is your care that you give to the work and to all that you do.
sentences.zh: 这也是它能流传50年的原因之一——我认为正是你对工作以及你所做的一切倾注的关怀，才让它历久弥新。

sentences.en: So thank you so much for everything.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢你所做的一切。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Please run it, guys.
sentences.zh: 请播放吧，伙计们。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You may have noticed something that we did not ask Robert Caro about, that many people want to know.
sentences.zh: 你们可能注意到了我们没有问罗伯特·卡罗（Robert Caro）的一件事，这也是许多人想知道的。

sentences.en: What happened to the chapter in The Power Broker that was devoted to Jane Jacobs?
sentences.zh: 《权力掮客》（The Power Broker）中关于简·雅各布斯（Jane Jacobs）的那一章去哪了？

sentences.en: So here's the backstory.
sentences.zh: 事情的背景是这样的。

sentences.en: Jane Jacobs was a journalist and activist who, in the 1950s, helped organize a successful opposition to the Lower Manhattan Expressway,
sentences.zh: 简·雅各布斯是一位记者兼活动家，她在20世纪50年代帮助组织了一场反对下曼哈顿高速公路的成功运动，

sentences.en: which would have cut through neighborhoods like Soho, Little Italy, and Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 那条高速公路本会穿过苏荷区、小意大利和唐人街等社区。

sentences.en: But Jacobs went on to write The Life and Death of Great American Cities,
sentences.zh: 但雅各布斯后来写了《美国大城市的死与生》（The Life and Death of Great American Cities），

sentences.en: this incredible book that delivers a withering critique of the urban renewal concepts and other harmful policies that Moses championed.
sentences.zh: 这本了不起的书对摩西所倡导的城市更新理念和其他有害政策进行了严厉的批判。

sentences.en: In the early stages of The Power Broker, Caro wrote about Jacobs' fight with Moses.
sentences.zh: 在《权力掮客》的早期阶段，卡罗确实写过雅各布斯与摩西的斗争。

sentences.en: But ultimately, her name does not appear in the book.
sentences.zh: 但最终，她的名字并没有出现在书中。

sentences.en: We didn't ask Caro about the Jane Jacobs chapter because he's been asked about this so many times, like over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我们没有问卡罗关于简·雅各布斯那一章的事，因为他已经被问过太多次了，一遍又一遍。

sentences.en: And his response is always, I can't remember what's in that chapter.
sentences.zh: 他的回答总是：我不记得那一章里写了什么。

sentences.en: But one of the last pieces in the New York Historical Society's exhibit is a letter from Jane Jacobs to Robert Caro from August 1974, shortly before the book was published.
sentences.zh: 但纽约历史学会展览中的最后几件展品之一，是简·雅各布斯在1974年8月写给罗伯特·卡罗的一封信，就在书出版前不久。

sentences.en: So it says, Dear Mr. Caro, many, many thanks for the copy of The Power Broker, which I treasure, and also for your too generous but much appreciated inscription.
sentences.zh: 信上写着：亲爱的卡罗先生，非常非常感谢您赠送的《权力掮客》，我视若珍宝，也感谢您那过于慷慨但令我深感荣幸的题词。

sentences.en: I have no doubt that many readers are going to feel the way I do.
sentences.zh: 我毫不怀疑，许多读者会有和我一样的感受。

sentences.en: We owe you a tremendous debt for all those years of work, good sense, unflagging curiosity, and compassion.
sentences.zh: 我们欠您一份巨大的债，感谢您多年来的工作、理智、不懈的好奇心和同情心。

sentences.en: I don't think anybody but a genuinely compassionate person, I do not mean sentimental, could have written that book.
sentences.zh: 我不认为除了一个真正富有同情心的人——我指的不是多愁善感——之外，还有谁能写出那本书。

sentences.en: What an account it is of human...
sentences.zh: 这是对人类……的何等记述啊。

sentences.en: Predicaments?
sentences.zh: 困境？

sentences.en: Yeah, predicaments, sorry.
sentences.zh: 是的，困境，抱歉。

sentences.en: There's like a little hyphen that goes into another word going up the side of it.
sentences.zh: 有一个小连字符连到了旁边的一行，接上了另一个词。

sentences.en: It's rare that you see a handwritten note where someone has a hyphen where they continue a word on the next line.
sentences.zh: 很少见到有人在手写笔记中用连字符把一个词拆分到下一行。

sentences.en: That's a writer.
sentences.zh: 那才是作家。

sentences.en: That's a real writer.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正的作家。

sentences.en: It is of human predicaments.
sentences.zh: 这是对人类困境的记述。

sentences.en: It ranks with the great novels in that respect.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，它足以与伟大的小说相媲美。

sentences.en: Well, you deserve a commensurate vacation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你理应享受一个相称的假期。

sentences.en: But Mary Nichols has told me that you are instead at work on a biography of LaGuardia.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽·尼科尔斯（Mary Nichols）告诉我，你反而正在撰写拉瓜迪亚（LaGuardia）的传记。

sentences.en: Selfishly, I can't help but be glad.
sentences.zh: 自私地说，我忍不住感到高兴。

sentences.en: I look forward to that.
sentences.zh: 我很期待那本书。

sentences.en: It's so much needs to be done, and nobody could do it as well.
sentences.zh: 有太多事情需要完成，没有人能比你做得更好。

sentences.en: Thank you again for sending the book, but especially for having written it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢你寄来这本书，但最重要的是感谢你当初写下了它。

sentences.en: Sincerely, Jane Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 诚挚的，简·雅各布斯。

sentences.en: I'm sorry to say, Jane Jacobs, he did not write that biography of LaGuardia.
sentences.zh: 很遗憾地告诉大家，简·雅各布斯，他最终没有写那本拉瓜迪亚的传记。

sentences.en: No, Jane Jacobs would go to her grave awaiting that LaGuardia biography.
sentences.zh: 不，简·雅各布斯直到去世也没能等到那本拉瓜迪亚传记。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Isabel Angel, edited by committee.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由伊莎贝尔·安吉尔（Isabel Angel）制作，委员会编辑。

sentences.en: Music by Swan Real, mixed by Martine Gonzalez.
sentences.zh: 音乐由Swan Real创作，马丁·冈萨雷斯（Martine Gonzalez）混音。

sentences.en: Special thanks to the folks at the New York Historical Society for making Elliot and my dreams come true.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢纽约历史学会的工作人员，让艾略特（Elliot）和我的梦想成真。

sentences.en: Kathy Tu is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 凯西·图（Kathy Tu）是我们的执行制片人。

sentences.en: Kurt Colstead is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯特德（Kurt Colstead）是数字总监。

sentences.en: Delaney Hall is our senior editor.
sentences.zh: 德莱尼·霍尔（Delaney Hall）是我们的高级编辑。

sentences.en: Taylor Cedric is our intern.
sentences.zh: 泰勒·塞德里克（Taylor Cedric）是我们的实习生。

sentences.en: The rest of the team includes Chris Berube, Jason DeLeon, Emmett Fitzgerald, Christopher Johnson, Vivian Leigh,
sentences.zh: 团队的其他成员包括克里斯·贝鲁贝（Chris Berube）、杰森·德里昂（Jason DeLeon）、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德（Emmett Fitzgerald）、克里斯托弗·约翰逊（Christopher Johnson）、薇薇安·李（Vivian Leigh），

sentences.en: Lasha Madon, Gabriella Gladney, Joe Rosenberg, Kelly Prime, Nina Potok, me, Roman Mars, and Jaka Medina Gleeson.
sentences.zh: 拉莎·马登（Lasha Madon）、加布里埃拉·格拉德尼（Gabriella Gladney）、乔·罗森伯格（Joe Rosenberg）、凯利·普莱姆（Kelly Prime）、妮娜·波托克（Nina Potok），还有我，罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars），以及雅卡·梅迪纳·格里森（Jaka Medina Gleeson）。

sentences.en: Congratulations to you and Billy, Jaka.
sentences.zh: 恭喜你和比利（Billy），雅卡。

sentences.en: It's just so nice to see two lovely young people get married and just, we're so happy for you.
sentences.zh: 看到两个可爱的年轻人结婚真是太好了，我们真为你感到高兴。

sentences.en: The 99% Invisible logo was created by Stephan Lawrence.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》的标志是由斯蒂芬·劳伦斯（Stephan Lawrence）设计的。

sentences.en: We are part of the Stitcher and SiriusXM podcast family, now headquartered six blocks north in the Pandora Building,
sentences.zh: 我们是Stitcher和SiriusXM播客家族的一员，现在总部位于北边六个街区外的潘多拉大厦（Pandora Building），

sentences.en: in beautiful Uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的住宅区。

sentences.en: You can find the show on all the usual social media sites as well as our own Discord server
sentences.zh: 你可以在所有常见的社交媒体网站上找到我们的节目，也可以加入我们的Discord服务器，

sentences.en: where we have a fun time talking about Power Broker, we talk about architecture, movies, and music, all kinds of good stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里愉快地讨论《权力掮客》，讨论建筑、电影、音乐，各种各样的好东西。

sentences.en: It's where I'm hanging out most of these days.
sentences.zh: 那是我最近待得最多的地方。

sentences.en: You can find a link to that Discord server every past episode of 99PI and catch up with the Power Broker breakdown at 99PI.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在99PI.org找到Discord服务器的链接、每一期往期节目，并补上《权力掮客》的深度解析。

sentences.en: I wonder what the inscription said.
sentences.zh: 我真想知道那上面的题词写了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我也想知道。

sentences.en: That would be something.
sentences.zh: 那一定很有意思。

sentences.en: I wonder if it was like, dear Jane, here's my book, you know, thanks for your part, sorry you're not in the book.
sentences.zh: 我在想是不是写着：亲爱的简，这是我的书，你知道的，感谢你的贡献，很抱歉你没能出现在书里。

sentences.en: Yeah, I wonder if there's part of the Jane Jacobs archive that has it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我在想简·雅各布斯的档案里会不会有这一部分。

sentences.en: This is that, now our next podcast series is the mystery of tracking down that inscription.
sentences.zh: 这就是了，我们下一个播客系列就是追踪那个题词的谜团。

sentences.en: And we'll do one of those episodes of a podcast where you follow the whole hunt and then you find it at the end
sentences.zh: 我们会做那种播客节目，带你追踪整个搜寻过程，然后在最后找到它，

sentences.en: and you could have just said what happened at the end.
sentences.zh: 虽然你本来可以直接说出最后发生了什么。

sentences.en: Or you find nothing, probably.
sentences.zh: 或者可能什么也找不到。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's more likely.
sentences.zh: 是的，那更有可能。

sentences.en: That's the podcast MO, is to make it all about the process because there is no answer.
sentences.zh: 这就是播客的套路，把重点放在过程上，因为根本就没有答案。

sentences.en: Something, the answer is truth or something?
sentences.zh: 什么，答案就是真相之类的？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: It turns out the answer was the friends we made along the way.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，答案是我们一路上结交的朋友。

sentences.en: The nature of truth and the friends we made along the way.
sentences.zh: 真相的本质，以及我们一路上结交的朋友。
